title: Cyclic Exif IFD pointers can exhaust CPU in libheif helper tools
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: The heif-dec, heif-thumbnailer and heif-enc helpers followed Exif IFD pointers recursively without a bound, so cyclic pointers could make processing consume excessive CPU. The library and gdk-pixbuf loader are not affected.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-TKUGU4GZ. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: The recursive traversal was replaced by a bounded iterative walk charged against Exif data size; fixed in libheif 1.23.7. Scope is the named helper tools. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: Crafted Exif with cyclic IFD pointers in heifio helper tools can cause excessive CPU while searching tags; affects heif-thumbnailer/heif-dec on HEIC/AVIF and heif-enc on JPEG/PNG, not library-only applications.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.
